curation_strategy: I first satisfied all three character arc obligations (6 for Reardon, 5 for Milvain, 4 for Marian) using high-interest passages that feature the arc character and carry the required dimension, distributing them across the segments where each arc is prominently demanded. Expert passages were then selected to cover each expert's primary dimensional demands—narrative technique and character development for Eleanor Hartley, social critique and atmosphere for James Blackstone, humour and close reading for Caroline Woodcourt—while structural passages filled the opening's thematic/social-critique gap. Diversity was maintained by drawing from different chapters and avoiding redundant selections within the same segment.

curation_assignments.rationale: Reardon's searing speech about society's indifference to struggling men launches the episode's central theme of the literary marketplace's brutality.
The narrator's defence of Reardon and Biffen as admirable in a humane society frames the social critique at the heart of the episode's opening.
Jasper's manifesto about incarnating the genius of vulgarity immediately establishes the commercial marketplace's demands as the episode's structuring tension.

curation_assignments.segment_name: The Architecture of Decline: Reardon's Spiral
curation_assignments.rationale: The vivid description of Reardon aged beyond his years by mental strain and deprivation opens his arc with a powerful image of physical collapse.

curation_assignments.segment_name: The Architecture of Decline: Reardon's Spiral
curation_assignments.rationale: Reardon's cyclical creative malady—grasping at story ideas that all collapse—captures the psychological mechanism of his decline with tragic precision.

curation_assignments.segment_name: The Architecture of Decline: Reardon's Spiral
curation_assignments.rationale: The morning scene of illegible corrections and collapsing syntax enacts Reardon's creative failure on the sentence level, ideal for narrative technique analysis.

curation_assignments.segment_name: The Architecture of Decline: Reardon's Spiral
curation_assignments.rationale: The tracing of how Amy's silence has broken Reardon's confidence in their marriage shows character development through relational deterioration.

curation_assignments.segment_name: The Architecture of Decline: Reardon's Spiral
curation_assignments.rationale: Reardon's own analysis of how happiness disrupted his development and led to intellectual failure gives the arc a powerful moment of self-awareness.

curation_assignments.segment_name: The Architecture of Decline: Reardon's Spiral
curation_assignments.rationale: Reardon's meditation on relative ideals and his inability to be insincere in his workmanship reveals the tragic integrity at the core of his decline.

curation_assignments.segment_name: The Architecture of Decline: Reardon's Spiral
curation_assignments.rationale: Reardon's philosophy that outliving one's reputation is a kind of death encapsulates his psychological collapse at peak tragic intensity.
Jasper's argument that most writers share his pragmatic views but conceal them provides sharp social critique of literary hypocrisy.
Jasper's defence of his unconventional path and his claim of a special faculty for extrapolating ideas establishes the self-serving logic of his ascent.
Jasper's definition of success as commanding cultivated pleasures lays bare the class aspirations driving his calculated rise.
Jasper's blunt declaration that nothing will impede his material advancement crystallises the moral compromise at the heart of his ascent.
Whelpdale's philosophy of targeting the quarter-educated mass extends the social critique of commercialism to the industrial production of cheap journalism.
The image of Jasper aged but triumphant, his manner suggesting meticulous care, shows the human cost of his successful ascent.
Jasper's lesson on inflating trivial ideas into verbal pyrotechnics for newspaper leaders shows the craft of cynical literary production.
Marian weeping in her room, reduced to 'a mere machine for reading and writing,' is the most concentrated image of her trapped condition.
The Museum passage where Marian questions the purpose of manufacturing literature captures her intellectual and emotional imprisonment.
Marian's candid perception of human hypocrisy and her resistance to illusion define the psychological complexity of her trapped position.
The image of labouring in the valley of the shadow of books for a ray of sunshine gives Marian's entrapment a tender, ironic poignancy perfect for close reading.
Marian's revulsion at literary rancour and the 'morbid excrescence' of literature articulates her entrapment between the literary world she serves and despises.
The gothicised Reading Room as prison, with readers as doomed flies, is a brilliantly atmospheric close-reading set piece for Marian's psychological state.
Biffen's theory of absolute realism—rejecting Zola's melodrama and Dickens's humour—provides rich material for narrative technique analysis.
Reardon's dread of unintelligent reviews that cannot address the true causes of his failure shows the literary market's inability to see what has been lost.
Reardon's condemnation of public-school writers incapable of understanding poverty frames the class politics of literary production and aesthetic judgment.
Biffen's argument that realist fiction should reject dramatic convention in favour of mundane reality—love scenes interrupted by illness—is a manifesto for anti-narrative.
The characterisation of Reardon as a man who cannot struggle against adverse conditions illuminates the fatal mismatch between his temperament and his market.
Reardon's ironic praise of his and Biffen's 'respectable' lack of vices is a comic highlight that satirises the absurdity of their virtuous poverty.
The novelist's exasperated reaction to classical scholarship and recommendation of fiction captures the comic absurdity of the literary marketplace.
The observation that both Jasper and Marian needed emotional relief, with Jasper performing cheerfulness, provides comic-ironic contrast before graver matters.

curation_assignments.segment_name: Closing: New Grub Street's Enduring Question
curation_assignments.rationale: Reardon's shabby clothes as both badge of degradation and source of bitter class identification closes the social arc with poignant ambiguity.

curation_assignments.segment_name: Closing: New Grub Street's Enduring Question
curation_assignments.rationale: Reardon's resolution to abandon literary pretence and seek remunerative work marks the final capitulation of his decline, completing the arc.

curation_assignments.segment_name: Closing: New Grub Street's Enduring Question
curation_assignments.rationale: The Dantean London fog as physical manifestation of Marian's anguish provides an atmospheric closing image that unites all three arcs in shared suffering.
